citation.title: Evolutionary de-homogenization using a generative model for optimizing solid-porous infill structures considering the stress concentration issue
citation.authors: Shuzhi Xu, Hiroki Kawabe, Kentaro Yaji

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The VAE-assisted method's tension-beam designs span a better peak-stress versus material-volume Pareto region than conventional stress-based topology optimization.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No ML-versus-classical runtime or speed-up is reported.
claim.alternatives: §4.2.2, Figure 19 gives quantitative Stress-TO comparisons with the non-ML low-fidelity initializer, rather than the VAE-assisted method; §5 summarizes a qualitative performance advantage.

baseline.problem_size: §4.2.1: 52×80 square elements in the low-fidelity tension-beam model
baseline.data_generation_cost: §4.2.2: 160 initial low-fidelity optimization results; computational cost not stated
baseline.quality_metric: §4.2.2–4.2.3: high-fidelity FE maximum von Mises stress, material volume fraction, Pareto hypervolume
baseline.quality_gap: §4.2.2, Figure 19: at about 13% volume, Stress-TO 3.05 MPa at 13.74% versus low-fidelity 2.64 MPa at 13.12%; at about 18%, 2.48 MPa at 18.11% versus 2.24 MPa at 17.89%. These figures compare the non-ML initialization with Stress-TO.

R2.evidence: §4.2.2–4.2.3: no classical timing baseline for a speed claim.

R4.evidence: §4.2.2–4.2.3: returned CAD designs receive high-fidelity FE stress analysis and volume fractions are reported, but failed or infeasible design rates are not given.

reporting.n_test_cases: §4: two 2D cases (L-bracket and tension beam); §4.2.2 compares 160 designs per method for the tension beam

notes: The paper's numerical Stress-TO comparison in §4.2.2 uses the non-ML low-fidelity initializer; the ML-assisted MFTD method is compared with Stress-TO by the Pareto plot in §4.2.3. The comparison concerns quality, not speed. §4 implementation states MATLAB 2022b and COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2, with TensorFlow for the VAE.
